name: manual_e89515
claim: Never use 'git checkout -- <file>' to undo a small test edit on a file that also has real uncommitted work — it discards ALL uncommitted changes to that file, not just the last edit.

decisions.notes: Mid-task on a Windows fresh-install session, an adversarial-test injection into discover.py was cleaned up with 'git checkout -- scripts/discover.py' intending to remove only the injected test line. Since the file's real fix was also uncommitted, the whole fix was silently discarded and the file reverted to the old buggy HEAD version. Caught only because a hygiene guard re-flagged the reverted file. Use 'git stash' or a diff-based revert (git apply -R, or manual re-edit) instead when a file has real uncommitted work mixed with a throwaway test change; commit real work before running any adversarial/destructive test on the same file.
